title: UGC Ad Scripts: 20 Templates for Hooks and Proof
summary: Use 20 UGC ad script templates for ecommerce, SaaS, and services, with visual beats, proof, CTAs, and a framework for controlled variants.
body_markdown:
A UGC ad script should specify what the viewer hears and sees. A practical structure is hook, situation, product, mechanism or demonstration, proof, and CTA. The best template depends on buyer awareness: a cold audience may need the problem explained, while retargeting can address an objection or offer directly.


Templates are starting structures. Replace every bracket with real audience language, approved facts, and visual evidence.


## Anatomy of a UGC script


Use four columns when writing:


Time Spoken line Visual/shot On-screen text


0–3s Hook Problem, result, or product action Short reinforcing phrase


3–8s Context Situation or workflow Who/what this is for


8–20s Product + proof Demonstration, UI, or evidence Key mechanism


20–30s CTA Result and next action Offer or action


If a line cannot produce a useful visual, rewrite it.


## Ecommerce script templates


### 1. Problem in progress


“If \[specific situation\] keeps causing \[specific problem\], watch this.” Show the problem, introduce the product, demonstrate the mechanism, and close with the relevant offer.


### 2. The routine upgrade


“The one thing I changed in my \[routine\] was…” Show the product inside the actual routine and name the concrete difference.


### 3. Live demonstration


“Here is what happens when…” Put the test on screen immediately. Avoid editing that hides the result.


### 4. Objection


“I thought \[objection\], but the part I missed was…” Answer with a feature or proof. Do not fabricate personal experience.


### 5. Honest fit


“This is useful if \[fit\], but skip it if \[non-fit\].” Explain the tradeoff and show the product.


### 6. Comparison


“Here is the difference between \[current method\] and \[product workflow\].” Compare supportable characteristics, not insults.


### 7. Three reasons


Open with the strongest reason, demonstrate each quickly, and avoid padding the list.


## SaaS and app script templates


### 8. Painful workflow


Show the old multi-step process, then the shorter product flow.


### 9. One-feature proof


“I can go from \[input\] to \[outcome\] without \[old step\].” Show the exact clicks or generated result.


### 10. Role-based use case


“If you manage \[job\], this removes \[specific task\].” Use screens that matter to that role.


### 11. Feature launch


“You can now \[new outcome\].” Lead with the user change, not company excitement.


### 12. Integration


“When \[trigger\] happens in \[tool\], \[product\] automatically \[action\].” Show the trigger and result.


### 13. Switching story


Compare workflows accurately and give the reason a specific user might switch.


## Service and info-product templates


### 14. Common mistake


Teach one error, explain its consequence, and show the mechanism the offer provides.


### 15. Mini-tutorial


Deliver a useful step before introducing the paid next action.


### 16. Myth and correction


Correct a specific misconception with evidence. Avoid manufacturing controversy.


### 17. Method preview


Show the first part of a real framework and who it is designed for.


### 18. FAQ


Answer a purchase-blocking question plainly, then point to the detailed page.


### 19. Proof-led explanation


Open with a verified result or demonstration and explain what caused it. State the source and limitations.


### 20. Retargeting reminder


Address the likely unresolved question after a product or pricing-page visit. Keep the promise and landing page aligned.
